messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — KV_CACHE_GROWTH / continuous-batching regression detected. Severity: P2. Trigger: sustained CPU and tail latency increase on inference-gang A. PagerDuty: https://pd/redwood/INC12345 :rotating_light:
morgan: noticed a slow ramp ~04:12 UTC, tail-latency spiking for hosts in us-west-2. KV cache size trending up, block-manager churn high. some requests hitting 1.5-2s instead of ~120ms. seeing OOMs on a couple canaries.
jin: thanks — adding context: recent rollout of continuous-batching v2 and block-manager tuning (block_size=64k) 02:30 UTC. Repro across canaries matching steady prefix-heavy workloads.
priya: are customers impacted? support-bot any alerts?
support-bot: Support alert: 5 customer escalations opened in last 15m for slow responses in /v1/generate. Top complainants: Acme, Novum. Errors are mostly timeouts and high latency.
alex: initial hypothesis: combination of larger block_size + more aggressive prefix KV caching causing metadata growth and cache eviction thrashing -> extra CPU + GC. continuous-batching amplifies it because more in-flight requests hold KV references longer.
morgan: current mitigation plan? we should avoid wide rollback if possible. need quick config toggles.
jin: propose immediate mitigations (fast):
- reduce continuous-batching max_batch_size to 8 and max_batch_latency_ms to 8
- set block_manager.block_size=32k (from 64k) for us-west pool via runtime-config (hot reload)
- temporarily enable eviction_policy=aggressive-size (fall back to LRU-after)
I can ship a config hotpatch in ~8-10m.
priya: +1. Also recommend enabling KV metadata TTL to 15m (was 6h) to curb leak while we investigate.
samir: can we throttle incoming traffic for affected routes? We have route-level throttles. I'd prefer to throttle heavy tenants rather than global degrade.
morgan: prioritize: 1) protect customers (throttle heavy tenants + fallback), 2) reduce memory growth, 3) stabilize tail latency.
alex: commands I'll run after jin pushes config:
```bash
# apply runtime config to us-west runtime cluster
redwoodctl runtime-config set --cluster us-west-2 --key continuous_batching.max_batch_size --value 8
redwoodctl runtime-config set --cluster us-west-2 --key continuous_batching.max_batch_latency_ms --value 8
redwoodctl runtime-config set --cluster us-west-2 --key block_manager.block_size --value 32768
redwoodctl runtime-config set --cluster us-west-2 --key block_manager.eviction_policy --value aggressive-size
```
Please watch rolling logs for 504s.
jin: patch pushed to staging and then us-west config will hot-reload. kicking off now.
incident-bot: RUNBOOK ACTION: Oncall handoff required in 30m if still unresoved. Assigned: morgan -> jin -> priya.
priya: monitoring: enabling KV cache metrics dashboard and increasing retention to 1h for alerting window. adding an anomaly detector on block_manager.metadata_size.
alex: after config change, we should also increase KV cache.log_level=DEBUG for 10m to capture eviction traces, then revert. I'll add the short window in the change description.
samir: throttles in place for top noisy customers (Acme, Novum) at 20rps per API key. Notified SEs.
support-bot: Notified affected customers with advisory template: "We're investigating increased latency for some requests; mitigations in progress."
morgan: incoming telemetry: after first config APPLIED (~04:28 UTC) — partial improvement in median latency but tail still bad on ~20% of hosts. memory growth rate reduced on most, but 3 pods still showing high metadata retention.
jin: for the 3 pods: collecting heap+proc maps, stack traces. suspect metadata references not being cleared during batched execution (KV reference counting bug).
priya: good that most nodes improved. For the 3 stubborn hosts, plan B: recycle pods after notifying coordinator. I'll prepare rolling restart for that subset to avoid global disruption.
alex: also enabling fallback router to route ~10% traffic for critical customers to smaller, non-cached model variant (stateless) to reduce stress while we root-cause.
morgan: agree. timeline: 04:35 config hotpatch applied, 04:40 throttles + customer notices, 04:45 targeted restart for 3 bad pods, 04:50 observe.
incident-bot: STATE CHANGE: Mitigation in progress. Incident updated.
jin: restarted the 3 pods (rolling, one at a time). After restart their metadata_size dropped 90% and tail latency recovered.
priya: monitoring now stable for 25m, overall P50/P95 close to baseline, P99 still ~1.1s on a small slice.
samir: customer impact update: Acme reports partial recovery; Novum still sees intermittent timeouts but improved. SEs are handling support tickets.
morgan: moving to recovery phase. Next steps: 1) full postmortem, 2) backport fix for reference counting in batch path, 3) permanent change: reduce default block_size to 32k for prefix-heavy workloads OR auto-tune, 4) add stricter metadata TTLs and observability (eviction traces).
alex: action items assigned: jin -> root-cause debug + PR for reference-count fix; priya -> add dashboards/alerts for metadata_size and eviction rate + playbook entry; samir -> evaluate safer throttle-as-code defaults; morgan -> coordinate postmortem + customer comms.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) at 04:58 UTC. Please file postmortem within 48h and tag with #kv-cache #block-manager #continuous-batching.
morgan: filing a short incident summary now and will link to the postmortem doc. Great fast work, team :heart:
